prs.title: [Packaging][Client] Add a staged lmcache-client build
prs.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Part 1 of #6315.

Adds `tools/client_wheel/`: `build.py` copies the tracked files that `manifest.toml` selects into a fresh staging root and builds an `lmcache-client` wheel there. The root build is unchanged. A CPU job builds the wheel in both boundary modes and checks that the checkout is unchanged.

- `manifest.toml`: `trees` and `files` say what ships (client, common, platform, transport, shared helpers, the SDK and the engine integrations). `[[exclude]]` takes shared files back out and always wins; each entry has an `owner` and a `reason` (today the six server-only `cache_context.py` hooks, #6310). A selected file under `deny` fails the build.
- `--boundary transitional` also ships the 64 server files the client still imports, grouped by the change that removes each. That wheel is a prototype.
- Static metadata, no console scripts; CUDA runtime packages are a `[cuda]` extra.

Validation (Linux x86_64, Python 3.13, torch 2.14.0+cpu, dev `3bfa771a`): both modes build and leave the checkout unchanged; the wheels ship the same 275/339 files and METADATA as the previous tooling builds from the same dev; a server file in `files` fails the build; pre-commit and actionlint with shellcheck pass. Not run: GPU, and this workflow on GitHub (build workflows skip drafts).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Replaces the units version of this PR (`55c7709f`). The four original commits are unchanged; the last one reads the manifest through `scope.py` and adds `[[exclude]]`.
- AI assistance was used. Design, code walkthrough and evidence are in the explainer.

prs.title: [Packaging][Client] Audit lmcache-client wheel contents and static imports
prs.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Part 2 of #6315. Stacked on #6582 (Part 1): the first five commits are #6582 and drop out once it merges; please review the last five.

Adds the static checks for the wheel #6582 builds and runs them in its CPU job. Both tools read `manifest.toml` through the same `scope.py` as the build.

- `audit.py` checks the wheel's files, compat shims, native extensions, METADATA and entry points against the staging record, `manifest.toml` and `tools/client_wheel/pyproject.toml`.
- `check_imports.py` follows every `lmcache` import of the non-server modules and fails on server files the boundary does not allow, on missing modules, and on an import of an `[[exclude]]` file that `boundary_gaps` does not list (the message names the entry's owner and reason). Third-party imports are checked against `pyproject.toml`. `--ratchet` keeps the transitional list exact.
- Dependencies: `+typing_extensions` (`security/api_key.py` imports it), `-psutil` (no shipped module imports it).
- CI: both audits, the transitional closure, the ratchet, and three counterexamples that must fail.

Validation (Linux x86_64, Python 3.13, dev `3bfa771a`): both audits report 0 failures; the transitional closure and the ratchet pass; the three counterexamples fail with their messages; the manifest-only variants behave as designed; the tools leave no `__pycache__` in the checkout.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Replaces the units version of this PR (`927be4c3`). The four original commits are unchanged apart from a context-only conflict in `manifest.toml`; the last one adapts them to #6582's manifest. The intermediate commits do not run on their own.
- `cryptography` is declared only for the `#6307 (#6509)` transitional group, so the PR that drops that group drops the dependency too.
- AI assistance was used. Design, code walkthrough and evidence are in the explainer.

prs.title: [CI][Client] Check lmcache-client in clean environments
prs.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Part 3 of #6315. Stacked on #6584 (Part 2) and #6582 (Part 1): the first ten commits are those PRs and drop out as they merge; please review the last six.

#6584 checks the wheel statically. This PR installs the wheels and checks them where they run.

- `check_imports.py --runtime`: every non-server module is imported in its own `python -I -B` process in a clean venv, then the manifest's `[smokes]` run (request clients, SDK, the legacy imports engines use). The strict wheel goes through the same check, report only, and is uploaded with its report.
- vLLM job: installs the CPU vLLM nightly that `cpu_device.yml` last verified, then requires every `lmcache.integration.vllm` module to import and vLLM's `LMCacheMPConnector` to resolve to the client's connector.
- `check_install.py`: a replace/uninstall matrix of the three lmcache distributions, and the client wheels as subsets of the full wheel.
- `tools/client_wheel/README.md`: what to edit to add, remove or exclude code, which check catches a missed edit, and what to remove once the migrations are done.

Validation (Linux x86_64, Python 3.13 and 3.12, dev `3bfa771a`): the clean-venv run imports 253 modules and 6 smokes with no failure; the strict report lists the 38 imports that still need server modules; the matrix and superset checks pass; the CPU and vLLM jobs pass when run from the workflow text.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Replaces the units version of this PR (`b3d7bfbe`). The five original commits are back (four with the same patch-id); the last one moves the smokes into the manifest and adds the strict-wheel report and the README.
- Removing the vLLM integration also means removing the vLLM job, which otherwise fails with `nothing to import`.
- AI assistance was used. Design, code walkthrough and evidence are in the explainer.

prs.title: [CI][Client] Build the lmcache-client CUDA profile
prs.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Part 4 of #6315. Stacked on #6594 (Part 3), #6584 (Part 2) and #6582 (Part 1): the first sixteen commits are those PRs and drop out as they merge; please review the last one.

The client CPU jobs build with `NO_GPU_EXT=1`, so the CUDA branch of `tools/client_wheel/setup.py` never runs in CI. This PR adds a compile-only `build-client-cuda` job. In `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.0` it builds the CUDA profile with the release `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`, audits the wheel, loads `cuda_ops` and `lmcache_native` without a GPU, and checks that removing `cuda_ops` from `native_allow` fails the build. It runs only when `pr_full_build.yml` calls the workflow with `cuda: true`. No GPU is needed; only the two workflow files change.

Validation: at this head, run locally in Docker from the workflow text (2 CPUs, one architecture), every `run:` step passes; the wheel is the CPU strict wheel's 275 files plus `cuda_ops`. Earlier, the same job passed in the fork with all 8 architectures in 9m33s ([run 43330713963](https://github.com/thegoldenflow/LMCache/actions/runs/43330713963)).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Replaces the units version of this PR (`28d6f881`); the commit is the same.
- Not run on GitHub at this head: drafts and PRs without `full` never reach the job.
- AI assistance was used. Design, cost and evidence are in the explainer.

prs.title: [CI][Client] Verify a client/server request across clean environments
prs.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Part 5 of #6315. Stacked on #6597 (Part 4), #6594 (Part 3), #6584 (Part 2) and #6582 (Part 1): the first seventeen commits are those PRs and drop out as they merge; please review the last three.

#6315's last runtime criterion is a real client/server request between separate clean environments, with cache reuse on the second request. `tools/client_wheel/check_e2e.py` does that for ZMQ and gRPC, with no inference engine: it starts `lmcache server` from the full wheel's venv, runs a client from the client wheel's venv (`python -I -B`, empty directory), and requires 0 hits on the cold lookup, a store, all 512 tokens hit on the second request, a byte-exact retrieve, every `lmcache` module loaded from the client venv, and a server that stops on SIGTERM and frees its ports. The CPU job runs it and uploads the report and logs as `client-e2e-logs`, also when the check fails.

Validation (Linux x86_64, Python 3.13, dev `3bfa771a`): ZMQ and gRPC both 0/512 cold and 512/512 on the second request, bytes equal; the CPU job passes from the workflow text; `pre-commit run --all-files` and actionlint with shellcheck pass.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The server may commit a store after replying to it, so the second lookup repeats under fresh request IDs for up to 10 s.
- Once #6307–#6310 land, the same check runs against the strict wheel by pointing `--client-python` at `venv-strict`.
- The first two commits come from the units version of this branch (`80ad31c4`, never opened as a PR); the third adds a shellcheck directive for the intended word splitting of `$gaps` and two rows to the README's cleanup table.
- AI assistance was used. Design, code walkthrough and evidence are in the explainer.
